statistical_testability_builds.effect_size_rationale: Prior work shows moderate influence of autonomic baseline on model calibration, suggesting a medium effect.
minimum_data_needed: average prediction interval width per subject
statistical_testability_builds.testable_prediction: Higher baseline HRV is associated with lower empirical coverage (negative direction) after adjusting for age, fitness level, and baseline stress reactivity.
statistical_testability_builds.failure_condition: If the adjusted association between baseline HRV and empirical coverage is not statistically significant (p >= 0.05) or the effect direction is positive or null.
statistical_testability_builds.statistical_test_plan: Perform linear regression of empirical coverage on baseline HRV, controlling for age, fitness level, and baseline stress reactivity; test the coefficient for baseline HRV; significance threshold p < 0.05; report beta and confidence interval.
statistical_testability_builds.statistical_testability_notes: Baseline HRV computed from first 5 min of ECG; coverage computed using Mondrian CP with calibration set from stress episodes; aim for at least 30 subjects to ensure adequate power.

statistical_testability_builds.effect_size_rationale: Effect size unknown until pilot data quantify the relationship between accelerometer high-frequency RMS and coverage decrement.
minimum_data_needed: accelerometer high-frequency RMS per time window
average prediction interval width per window
statistical_testability_builds.testable_prediction: Increase in accelerometer high-frequency RMS leads to decrease in empirical coverage (negative direction).
statistical_testability_builds.failure_condition: If no significant negative correlation between accelerometer high-frequency RMS and empirical coverage after controlling for attachment quality, BMI, and activity type.
statistical_testability_builds.statistical_test_plan: Compute Pearson correlation (or linear mixed-effects model with subject as random effect) between accelerometer high-frequency RMS and empirical coverage across windows; test significance p < 0.05; include attachment quality, BMI, activity type as covariates.
statistical_testability_builds.statistical_testability_notes: Use window size e.g., 10s; ensure sufficient artifact variability; exclude periods with low signal quality.

statistical_testability_builds.effect_size_rationale: Habituation effects in physiological responses are typically moderate, suggesting a medium effect size.
minimum_data_needed: time since recording start (min) per segment
average prediction interval width per bin
statistical_testability_builds.testable_prediction: Later recording time (greater minutes since start) is associated with lower empirical coverage (negative direction).
statistical_testability_builds.failure_condition: If the slope of coverage vs time is not significantly negative after controlling for time of day, fatigue score, and annotator experience.
statistical_testability_builds.statistical_test_plan: Split recording into equal time bins (e.g., 5-min); compute coverage per bin; run linear regression of coverage on bin midpoint controlling for time of day, fatigue score, annotator experience; test coefficient for time.
statistical_testability_builds.statistical_testability_notes: Ensure at least 6 bins per subject to capture trend; use mixed-effects model with subject random intercept.

statistical_testability_builds.effect_size_rationale: Timestamp synchronization errors are expected to have a small but detectable impact on coverage.
minimum_data_needed: timestamp offset between ECG and respiration (ms) per segment
average prediction interval width per segment
statistical_testability_builds.testable_prediction: Larger absolute timestamp offset leads to lower empirical coverage (negative direction).
statistical_testability_builds.failure_condition: If no significant negative correlation between offset magnitude and coverage after controlling for hardware latency jitter, signal quality index, and movement artifact level.
statistical_testability_builds.statistical_test_plan: Estimate offset per segment via mutual information maximization; compute coverage per segment; run linear regression of coverage on absolute offset controlling for latency jitter, SQI, movement artifact; test significance.
statistical_testability_builds.statistical_testability_notes: Require at least 20 segments with both signals present; ensure sampling rates >=130 Hz ECG, >=70 Hz respiration.

statistical_testability_builds.effect_size_rationale: Effect size unknown until inter-annotator disagreement data are collected to quantify label noise impact.
minimum_data_needed: label noise entropy (inter-annotator disagreement) per segment
average prediction interval width per segment
statistical_testability_builds.testable_prediction: Higher label noise entropy leads to lower empirical coverage (negative direction).
statistical_testability_builds.failure_condition: If no significant negative correlation between label entropy and coverage after controlling for annotator expertise, stimulus ambiguity, and inter-annotator agreement variability.
statistical_testability_builds.statistical_test_plan: Compute label entropy per segment from multiple annotators; compute coverage per segment; run linear regression of coverage on entropy controlling for expertise score, stimulus clarity rating, kappa; test significance.
statistical_testability_builds.statistical_testability_notes: If multiple labels unavailable, simulate label noise by flipping a proportion of labels according to estimated error rate; need at least 30 segments with multiple annotations.

statistical_testability_builds.effect_size_rationale: Baseline arousal shifts are expected to produce a moderate effect on coverage when stratification ignores subject-specific offsets.
minimum_data_needed: subject baseline arousal (mean skin conductance level)
average prediction interval width per group
statistical_testability_builds.testable_prediction: Lower baseline arousal leads to lower empirical coverage (negative direction) when using high-intensity stratum.
statistical_testability_builds.failure_condition: If after adjusting for baseline measurement duration, stress episode count, and baseline GSR variability, the association between baseline arousal and coverage is not significant.
statistical_testability_builds.statistical_test_plan: Group subjects by baseline arousal (e.g., low vs high tertiles); compute coverage per group within each stress intensity stratum; run linear regression of coverage on baseline arousal controlling for baseline measurement duration, episode count, baseline GSR variability; test significance.
statistical_testability_builds.statistical_testability_notes: Baseline measured during 5-min resting period before each stress episode; aim for at least 15 subjects per baseline group.

statistical_testability_builds.effect_size_rationale: Small calibration sets are known to cause substantial quantile estimation error, suggesting a large effect on coverage.
minimum_data_needed: number of calibration samples per subject
average prediction interval width per subject
quantile confidence interval width per subject
statistical_testability_builds.testable_prediction: Fewer calibration samples lead to lower empirical coverage (negative direction).
statistical_testability_builds.failure_condition: If after controlling for stress episode count, labeling consistency, and total recording duration, the association between calibration size and coverage is not significant.
statistical_testability_builds.statistical_test_plan: Compute calibration size per subject; run linear regression of coverage on calibration size controlling for stress episode count, labeling consistency (kappa), total recording duration; test coefficient significance; additionally use bootstrap to estimate quantile variance.
statistical_testability_builds.statistical_testability_notes: Minimum of 10 samples required for stable quantile; ensure at least 20 subjects spanning the calibration size spectrum.

statistical_testability_builds.effect_size_rationale: Effect size unknown until pilot data assess the impact of missing GSR-temperature interaction on coverage.
minimum_data_needed: galvanic skin response (GSR) per time point
interaction term (GSR * temperature) per time point
average prediction interval width per subject
statistical_testability_builds.testable_prediction: Stronger GSR-temperature interaction (higher product) leads to lower empirical coverage (negative direction).
statistical_testability_builds.failure_condition: If after controlling for overall GSR amplitude, temperature range, and motion artifact level, the association between the interaction term and coverage is not significant.
statistical_testability_builds.statistical_test_plan: Fit linear scoring function; compute residuals; compute empirical coverage per subject; test interaction term significance via hierarchical regression: add interaction term to model and evaluate change in coverage error using F-test; alternatively regress coverage on interaction term controlling for GSR amplitude, temperature range, artifact level.
statistical_testability_builds.statistical_testability_notes: Require periods where both GSR and temperature vary (e.g., during stress); sampling rate >=4 Hz for each; aim for at least 25 subjects with sufficient variation.

statistical_testability_builds.effect_size_rationale: Substance effects on physiological dynamics are expected to be modest, suggesting a small effect size.
minimum_data_needed: average prediction interval width per group
statistical_testability_builds.testable_prediction: Presence of caffeine/medication leads to lower empirical coverage (negative direction).
statistical_testability_builds.failure_condition: If after adjusting for time of day, baseline stress level, and age, the association between substance intake and coverage is not significant.
statistical_testability_builds.statistical_test_plan: Divide subjects into substance users vs non-users; compute coverage per group; run linear regression of coverage on substance indicator controlling for time of day (circadian phase), baseline stress (pre-task HRV), age; test coefficient significance.
statistical_testability_builds.statistical_testability_notes: Collect self-report within 2h before recording; if unavailable, use metabolite assays; ensure at least 10 users and 10 non-users.

statistical_testability_builds.effect_size_rationale: Edge effects from fixed-window feature extraction are expected to produce a moderate impact on coverage for short bouts.
minimum_data_needed: empirical coverage for bouts < window length
empirical coverage for bouts >= window length
average prediction interval width per bout duration bin
statistical_testability_builds.testable_prediction: Shorter bout length relative to window leads to lower empirical coverage (negative direction).
statistical_testability_builds.failure_condition: If after controlling for label ambiguity, bout duration variance, and feature extraction method, the association between bout duration/window ratio and coverage is not significant.
statistical_testability_builds.statistical_test_plan: Compute bout duration and window length; compute coverage per bout; run linear regression of coverage on bout duration/window ratio controlling for label ambiguity score, bout duration variance, feature method type; test significance; additionally compare coverage between short bouts (< window) and long bouts (>= window) using independent-samples t-test.
statistical_testability_builds.statistical_testability_notes: Stress bouts defined by annotation epochs; fixed window length used for feature extraction (e.g., 10s); ensure sufficient number of short and long bouts (>15 each).
